stdout_tail:
Analysis complete. `analysis.py` and `result.json` are written in the working directory.

**Finding:** Model family has a modest but consistent effect on this dataset. Comparing four families with matched preprocessing (Logistic Regression, KNN, Random Forest, Hist Gradient Boosting) under 5-fold CV + held-out test evaluation:

| Model | Test ROC-AUC | Test Accuracy |
|---|---|---|
| KNN (k=25) | 0.894 | 0.848 |
| Logistic Regression | 0.906 | 0.854 |
| Random Forest | 0.919 | 0.867 |
| HistGradientBoosting | **0.930** | **0.876** |

Boosted/bagged tree ensembles beat linear and instance-based models by a real but modest margin (ROC-AUC spread ≈ 0.035, i.e. ~3.5 points). CV standard deviations (0.002–0.005) are much smaller than this spread, so the ranking is not noise. All four models comfortably beat the majority-class baseline (0.761 accuracy), meaning family choice matters far less than using any reasonably-configured model at all.

parsed_result.summary: Model family has a modest but real effect on predictive performance: test ROC-AUC ranges from 0.894 (KNN) to 0.930 (HistGradientBoosting), a spread of 0.035. The boosted/bagged tree ensembles (RandomForest, HistGradientBoosting) modestly but consistently outperform the linear (LogisticRegression) and instance-based (KNN) models, though all four clear the majority-class baseline (0.761 accuracy) by a wide margin, so the choice of family matters far less than simply using a reasonably-tuned model at all.
parsed_result.primary_metric_name: ROC-AUC range across model families (best - worst, test set)
parsed_result.methodological_choices: 80/20 stratified train/test split (seed=42) plus 5-fold stratified CV on the training set as a robustness check; final numbers reported on the held-out test set. Missing categorical values (workclass, occupation, native-country) imputed as an explicit 'Missing' category rather than dropped. Categoricals one-hot encoded, numerics standardized, identically for all four models (harmless for tree models, needed for LogisticRegression/KNN) so the comparison isolates model family rather than preprocessing. Compared 4 model families representing different inductive biases: LogisticRegression (linear), KNN (k=25, instance-based), RandomForest (300 trees, bagging), HistGradientBoosting (boosting) — all near-default hyperparameters, no per-model tuning via grid/random search, since the question is about family choice, not tuning effort. ROC-AUC chosen as primary metric over accuracy because the target is imbalanced (~24% positive); accuracy and F1 reported as secondary metrics. No explicit class-imbalance handling (e.g. class_weight, SMOTE) was applied — all models used their default handling of the ~76/24 class split.
